AI screening only; methodological problems do not establish misconduct.

**Context and coverage.** This classifier study evaluates held-out prediction through splitting, preprocessing and tuning. Completed: C1–C4 procedural review. Not assessed: implementation, data quality, numerical reproduction, uncertainty or effect size; code, data, predictions and seeds are absent. Only file tools were used; no code or benchmarks ran.

**F01 — test information enters preprocessing (C2).** Standardization includes test records. Reproduce by tracing rows determining preprocessing parameters; then fit the scaler only on training data and apply it unchanged to held-out data. Assuming prediction on unseen records is intended, this compromises isolation. A benign explanation is preprocessing convenience or an intended transductive setting; clarify the setting. Direction and size of score changes are unknown.

**F02 — test-set reuse for selection (C3).** The same score chooses hyperparameters and serves as final evaluation. Verify the search/evaluation log and identify any untouched final set. Under the stated held-out claim, this score is selection-dependent and cannot independently assess the chosen configuration. A benign explanation is calling a validation set “test”; C3 describes no final independent evaluation.

**Counterevidence and next checks.** C1 reports a split, but splitting alone does not resolve either issue. Refit preprocessing inside training/validation folds, tune there, and evaluate once on an untouched set; compare the resulting performance without assuming its outcome.
